question: If for a group of 20 items, Σx = 1452, Σx² = 144280 and mode = 63.7, then Pearsonian coefficient of skewness is equal to
solution:
The correct answer is** 0.202**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pearsonian coefficient of skewness is calculated using the formula:** less Copy code

 
 
• The formula of *Skewness = (Mean - Mode) / Standard Deviation*.
 
• To calculate the mean: Divide the sum of the values (Σx) by the total number of items (N). In this case, Σx = 1452 and N = 20, giving a mean of 72.6.
 
• To calculate the standard deviation: Use the formula *SD = √[(Σx² / N) - Mean²]*. Here, Σx² = 144280, and N = 20, resulting in SD = √1936.24 = 44.
 
• Finally, substitute the values into the formula for skewness: (72.6 - 63.7) / 44 = 0.202.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Skewness in financial enterprises:**

 
 
• Skewness helps in understanding the distribution of financial data. Positive skewness indicates a longer tail on the right, often seen in stock returns with rare, large gains.
 
• Negative skewness implies a longer tail on the left, suggesting frequent smaller losses and occasional large losses, typical in risk assessments.
 
• In financial data analysis, skewness is crucial for evaluating asymmetry in distributions, affecting decision-making processes for risk management.
